title: GP7a spike — the assessed-value shadow ledger: tax-rate x seed sweep, measured on the UNCHANGED build

meta.measured_on: b3d780c (unchanged) — git worktree of the pinned baseline; js/ index.html css/ byte-identical to the working tree at measurement time
meta.harness: node 22 vm context loading js/sim.js verbatim (sim.js is DOM-free); Math.random UNSTUBBED; no RNG stub anywhere
meta.note: c.taxRate = rate is re-asserted every tick because the pinned build_script never sets it and index.html:143 pins the slider to 0..20.

saturation.definition: medianRaw_* is the median across the 20 corpus seeds of the PRE-CLAMP demand bar (summed left-to-right in source order, exactly as demandBreakdown does, so parts-sum-reproduces-raw holds). clampedSeeds_* counts how many of the 20 seeds have that bar sitting against clampD's [-1,1] bound.

verdict: jobsAvail/220 is the binding term on the residential bar: at the reference rate 7 it supplies a median 2.679 of the bar's 2.797 pre-clamp raw while taxMod contributes exactly 0.00, and clampD's +1 ceiling holds on all 20 seeds until rate 15 and on at least one seed until rate 18 — the first rate at which no seed is clamped is 19; the commercial and industrial bars are never clamped at any rate 0..20.
drift_findings: taxMod = (7 - rate) * 0.05 is STRICTLY LINEAR over the whole shipped 0..20 slider and peaks at |0.65| (rate 20) against clampD's [-1,1]. It is therefore not broken and needs no repair: GP7b's curve work is a SHAPE CHOICE, not a fix.

Because the residential bar is saturated at every rate below 15 on the reference corpus, a numeric elasticity d(demand.r)/d(taxMod) measured at the reference equilibrium reports exactly 0 — which is why quality_gates[1]'s elasticity clause is unmeasurable on an unchanged build and is replaced here by the published pre-clamp raw, headroom, clamped flag and the two candidate terms.

meanTakeWindow is non-monotonic in the rate: it rises to a median 26,867 at rate 14 and then COLLAPSES (15,539 at 15; 116 at 20) as the city depopulates. The revenue-maximising rate on this corpus is 14, not 20.
At rate 0 the take is identically 0 for every seed (there is no assessed floor today). GP7b's floor question therefore has a published reference point.

fixtures.note: Committed VERBATIM so G6 is reproducible from this file. Both share an IDENTICAL water / civics / road / zoning-band scaffold; only power cleanliness, parks and wonder landmarks differ. Measured on b3d780c with the GP7a assessment constants (ASSESS_* = the headcount coefficients, assessmentAt(v) = 0.5 + v/128) replicated harness-side, because assessedLedger() does not exist on the unchanged build.
fixtures.deviation_from_design: The design's authored band split (PRIME zr above y=42 / zc below; CHEAP zr y<24 / zi) was MEASURED to deadlock PRIME at pop 536 / 104 developed lots: with no industrial band there is no +0.28 export base, so jobsAvail goes negative and both bars sit under the 0.15 growth gate. Both fixtures therefore use the pinned baseline's three-band split (zr y<30, zc y<52, zi y>=52), which makes the comparison a controlled one — the ONLY authored difference is what drives land value.
